gloss: be good, pleasing; go well; good, fine, fair; better; good things, welfare, goodness
summary: The root is what is good: pleasing to the senses, sound and fit for use, glad of heart, right, and so welcome and approved. God sees each work of the six days “that it was טוֹב”, and all of it “טוֹב מְאֹד” (Gen 1:31); a land, gold or figs are good in quality, a face fair, a heart merry with a feast, and what is “good in the eyes” of someone is what pleases him. Morally טוֹב is what God shows man and requires (Mic 6:8), set against רַע; and Yahweh himself is good, his goodness shown in what he does (Psa 119:68; Exo 33:19). The nouns are the good that comes to or is done for someone, welfare and good things; the verb יָטַב, with its own root, is to be good or go well, and in its hiphil to do good to someone or to do a thing well (Num 10:29, 32).

words.gloss: good: fine, fit; fair; pleasing; glad; right; better (than)
words.summary: By far the commonest word of the root. Its uses run from the plainly physical (good gold, good figs, a fair face) through what pleases or is approved (“good in your eyes”) and gladness of heart, to what is morally right and to God’s own goodness. With מִן it is “better than”, the usual way Hebrew compares.

senses.gloss: good in quality, fine, fit for use
senses.definition: Sound and of good kind: gold, land, fruit, grain, wine or an animal that is as it should be, the opposite of what is רַע, bad, unfit.

evidence.note: One basket of “very טֹבוֹת figs, like first-ripe figs”, the other of “very רָעוֹת figs, which cannot be eaten for badness”.
“The gold of that land is טוֹב.”
A vowed animal is not to be exchanged, “טוֹב for רַע or רַע for טוֹב”.
The priest values it “between טוֹב and רַע”.
The spies are to see “whether the land is טוֹבָה or רָעָה”.
Joshua and Caleb: “the land … is exceedingly, exceedingly טוֹבָה”.
“A טוֹבָה land, a land of streams of water.”
“A land טוֹבָה and broad, flowing with milk and honey.”
Seven ears of grain, fat and טֹבוֹת.
A calf “tender and טוֹב”.
“Your palate like the טוֹב wine”: the best.
“Every טוֹב tree” and “every טוֹבָה portion of land”: the best.

senses.definition: Of persons, good to look at, handsome or beautiful; often with מַרְאֶה, “appearance”, and beside יָפֶה, “beautiful”.

evidence.note: Rebekah, “טֹבַת מַרְאֶה, very”: very fair to look at.
David, “ruddy, with beautiful (יְפֵה) eyes and טוֹב רֹאִי, good to see”.
The sons of God saw the daughters of men “that they were טֹבֹת”.
Moses’ mother saw “that he was טוֹב” and hid him.
Saul, “a young man and טוֹב; there was none among the sons of Israel טוֹב more than he”.
Esther, “fair of form and טוֹבַת מַרְאֶה”.

senses.definition: God’s judgment on each thing he made in the six days: it was as he meant it, with nothing wrong in it; and of the whole, “very good”.

evidence.note: “God saw the light, that it was טוֹב.”
“God saw all that he had made, and behold, טוֹב מְאֹד”: on the sixth day, the whole.
Every tree “desirable to see and טוֹב for food”.
“It is לֹא טוֹב that the man should be alone”: the one thing called not good, and God at once makes the woman.

senses.gloss: pleasing, agreeable; what seems good (to someone)
senses.definition: What pleases a person or meets his approval, usually “good in the eyes of” or “good to” someone; “do what is good in your eyes” is “do as you think best”.

evidence.note: “Your maid is in your hand; do to her הַטּוֹב בְּעֵינָיִךְ.”
Eli: “It is Yahweh; let him do הַטּוֹב בְּעֵינָיו.”
The daughters of Zelophehad may marry “whom it is טוֹב in their eyes”, within their tribe.
Balaam saw “that it was טוֹב in the eyes of Yahweh to bless Israel”.
“If it is טוֹב to the king”: the courtier’s formula for a request.
“You shall do הַיָּשָׁר וְהַטּוֹב in the eyes of Yahweh”: what he approves.
Achish to David: “your going out and coming in with me is טוֹב in my eyes”.
“How טוֹב and how pleasant (נָּעִים) for brothers to dwell together.”

senses.definition: Of the heart, glad and cheerful, often with food and wine; of a day, a feast day, a day of gladness.

evidence.note: After the feast the people went home “glad (שְׂמֵחִים) and טוֹבֵי לֵב for all the good Yahweh had done”.
“All the days of the afflicted are evil, but the טוֹב לֵב has a continual feast.”
Haman went out “glad and טוֹב לֵב”.
David’s men “have come on a יוֹם טוֹב”: a feast day, at the sheep-shearing.
“Gladness and joy for the Jews, a feast and a יוֹם טוֹב.”
The fourteenth of Adar kept as “gladness and feasting and a יוֹם טוֹב”.
The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months are to become “joy and gladness and מֹעֲדִים טוֹבִים” for Judah: glad appointed feasts.
“Drink your wine with a טוֹב heart.”

senses.definition: What is right in God’s sight and in dealings with others, set against רַע, evil; and a man who does it.

evidence.note: “He has told you, O man, מַה־טּוֹב, and what Yahweh requires of you: to do justice, to love חֶסֶד, and to walk humbly with your God.”
“Seek טוֹב and not רָע, that you may live.”
“Hate רָע and love טוֹב, and establish justice in the gate.”
“Woe to those who call רָע טוֹב and טוֹב רָע”, set beside darkness for light and bitter for sweet.
“Haters of טוֹב and lovers of רָע.”
Samuel will teach them “the טוֹבָה and the יְשָׁרָה way”.
“Ask for the ancient paths, where is the way of הַטּוֹב, and walk in it.”
“A טוֹב man obtains favour from Yahweh, but a man of wicked schemes he condemns.”
“He is a טוֹב man and comes with טוֹבָה news.”
“Do good, Yahweh, to the טוֹבִים, and to the upright in their hearts.”
At Sinai God gave “upright judgments, true laws, טוֹבִים statutes and commandments”.

senses.gloss: good (of Yahweh, his name, spirit and word)
senses.definition: Yahweh is good: kind and faithful toward his people and all he has made, as his works and his חֶסֶד show; his name, spirit and word are good.

evidence.note: “Give thanks to Yahweh, כִּי־טוֹב, for his חֶסֶד is forever”: the refrain of the temple’s praise.
Sung when the foundation of the second house was laid.
To be sung again in the restored land.
“For Yahweh is טוֹב; his חֶסֶד is forever, and his faithfulness to all generations.”
“You are טוֹב and do good (מֵטִיב); teach me your statutes”: his goodness shown in what he does.
“Yahweh is טוֹב to all, and his compassion is over all his works.”
“טוֹב and upright is Yahweh; therefore he instructs sinners in the way.”
“Taste and see that Yahweh is טוֹב; blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.” Quoted 1Pe 2:3.
“You, Lord, are טוֹב and ready to forgive.”
“Yahweh is טוֹב, a stronghold in the day of trouble.”
“Yahweh is טוֹב to those who wait for him.”
“Surely God is טוֹב to Israel, to the pure in heart.”
“I will wait on your name, for it is טוֹב.”
“Your spirit is טוֹבָה; lead me in a level land.” Also Neh 9:20.
“Your judgments are טוֹבִים.”

senses.definition: With מִן, “good beyond”, which is how Hebrew says “better than”; the proverbs’ “better is … than …” weigh one good against another.

evidence.note: “To obey is טוֹב מִזֶּבַח”, better than sacrifice.
“טוֹב to take refuge in Yahweh than to trust in man.”
“Your חֶסֶד is טוֹב מֵחַיִּים”, better than life.
“A day in your courts is טוֹב than a thousand.”
“טוֹב a little with the fear of Yahweh than great treasure and trouble with it.”
“טוֹב is one slow to anger than the mighty.”
“A good name is טוֹב than טוֹב ointment”: both uses in one line.
“It would be טוֹב for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
“My death is טוֹב than my life.”

senses.gloss: good (and evil): to know, discern or choose
senses.definition: Paired with רַע in “to know (or discern) good and evil”: the power to judge for oneself what is good and what is bad, which little children lack and a judge must have.

evidence.note: “The tree of the knowledge of טוֹב וָרָע.”
The serpent: “you will be like God, knowing טוֹב וָרָע”.
“The man has become like one of us, to know טוֹב וָרָע.”
“Your children, who today do not know טוֹב וָרָע”: too young to choose.
Immanuel will eat curds and honey “until he knows to refuse the evil and choose הַטּוֹב”.
Solomon asks “a hearing heart to judge your people, to discern between טוֹב and רָע”.
“As the angel of God, so is my lord the king, to hear הַטּוֹב וְהָרָע.”
Barzillai at eighty: “can I discern between טוֹב and רָע? can your servant taste what I eat?”

parallels.note: “Upright, right”: “the right and the good in the eyes of Yahweh”; “good and upright is Yahweh”.
Yahweh’s steadfast kindness, named with his goodness in the refrain “for he is good, for his חֶסֶד is forever”.
“Beautiful”, beside it of a fair person.

opposites.note: Bad, evil: the root’s constant opposite, of figs, animals and land as of deeds and men.

phrases.gloss: good in the eyes of: pleasing to, approved by
give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good
a good day: a feast day, holiday
the good hand of my God (upon me)

evidence.locator: Gen.1.4, טוֹב → καλόν; Gen.2.9, טוֹב → καλόν, καλοῦ; Mic.6.8, טּוֹב → καλόν; καλός renders טוֹב ×84

evidence.note: “Every creature of God is καλόν, and nothing to be refused if received with thanksgiving”: Gen 1’s word for what God made.
The mature, “by use having their senses trained to discern καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ”: the טוֹב וָרָע of Gen 2:9 and 1Ki 3:9.

evidence.locator: Psa.34.13, טוֹב → ἀγαθάς; Isa.7.15, טּוֹב → ἀγαθόν; ἀγαθός renders טוֹב ×269

evidence.note: Quotes Psa 34:13: “he who would love life and see ἡμέρας ἀγαθάς”.
“Why do you call me ἀγαθόν? No one is ἀγαθός but one, God.” Also Mrk 10:18.

evidence.locator: Psa.34.9, טוֹב → χρηστός; Psa.106.1 and Psa.119.68 the same; χρηστός renders טוֹב ×21

evidence.note: “If you have tasted that the Lord is χρηστός”: Psa 34:9, “taste and see that Yahweh is טוֹב”.
The Most High “is χρηστός to the unthankful and evil”.

words.gloss: good, good things; welfare, prosperity; good news
words.summary: The adjective used as a noun: “the good”, what is good for a person, the good things that fill and satisfy him, and the good done or spoken. Its forms are spelled as the adjective’s, so which uses are the noun is read from the sense.

senses.definition: What is good for a person: food and plenty, peace and prosperity, the good that God gives or withholds; the opposite of the evil that comes on someone.

evidence.note: “Young lions lack and hunger, but those who seek Yahweh will not lack any טוֹב.”
“Yahweh will not withhold טוֹב from those who walk whole.”
“Who satisfies your mouth with טוֹב.”
He fills the hungry soul with טוֹב.
“Who will show us טוֹב? Lift up the light of your face on us, Yahweh.”
“I hoped for טוֹב, and רָע came; I waited for light, and darkness came.”
“We waited for peace, and there is no טוֹב.” Also Jer 14:19.
“Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with טוֹב.”
To eat and drink “and make his soul see טוֹב in his labour”.
Yahweh’s commandments, “which I command you today לְטוֹב לָךְ”, for your good.
“Surely טוֹב and חֶסֶד shall pursue me all the days of my life.”
“Israel has cast off טוֹב; the enemy shall pursue him.”

senses.definition: The good someone speaks concerning another: a promise of good, or good news.

evidence.note: Moses to Hobab: “Come with us and we will do you good, for Yahweh has spoken טוֹב concerning Israel”: the place he said he would give them.
“That טוֹב which Yahweh will do with us, the same we will do to you.”
“How beautiful on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news … who brings good news of טוֹב, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, ‘Your God reigns.’” Quoted Rom 10:15.
Micaiah “does not prophesy טוֹב concerning me, but evil”.

senses.gloss: good (as done): good deeds, what is right
senses.definition: The good a person does, as object of עָשָׂה, “do”: right conduct, set against evil.

evidence.note: “Turn from evil and do טוֹב; seek peace and pursue it.” Quoted 1Pe 3:11.
“Turn from evil and do טוֹב, and dwell forever.”
“Trust in Yahweh and do טוֹב.”
“There is none who does טוֹב.” Also Psa 14:3 and 53:2, 4; Rom 3:12.
“There is not a righteous man on earth who does טוֹב and does not sin.”
They are adversaries to me “because I pursue טוֹב”.

evidence.locator: Isa.52.7, טוֹב → ἀγαθά; Psa.34.15, טוֹב → ἀγαθόν; Psa.84.12, טוֹב → ἀγαθά; Num.10.32, טּוֹב → ἀγαθά

evidence.note: Quotes Isa 52:7: “how beautiful the feet of those who bring good news of τὰ ἀγαθά”; the Peshitta has ܛܒܬܐ, this root.
Quotes Psa 34:15: “let him turn from evil and do ἀγαθόν”.

evidence.locator: Psa.14.3, טוֹב → χρηστότητα

evidence.note: Quotes Psa 14:3: “there is none who does χρηστότητα, not even one”.

words.gloss: good done, kindness, benefit; welfare, prosperity; the good promised
words.summary: The feminine noun: the good done to someone, a kindness or benefit; someone’s welfare and prosperity; and, with God as speaker, the good he has promised. לְטוֹבָה is “for good”. Its spelling is also the adjective’s feminine, so its uses are told from the sense.

senses.definition: A good deed done for someone, which should be repaid with good; repaying evil for it is the mark of the wicked.

evidence.note: Saul to David: “You have repaid me הַטּוֹבָה, and I have repaid you הָרָעָה.”
“Whoever returns evil for טוֹבָה, evil will not depart from his house.”
“They repay me evil for טוֹבָה.” Also Psa 38:21; 109:5.
They did not show חֶסֶד to Gideon’s house “according to all the טוֹבָה he had done for Israel”.
Jehoiada buried among the kings “because he had done טוֹבָה in Israel, toward God and his house”.
They reported Tobiah’s טוֹבֹת, his good deeds, before Nehemiah.
Evil-merodach “spoke טֹבוֹת with” Jehoiachin: kindly.

senses.definition: Someone’s good estate: peace and prosperity sought for him, goods increasing, a day of good fortune.

evidence.note: Of Ammon and Moab: “You shall not seek their peace (שְׁלֹמָם) or their טוֹבָה all your days.”
It grieved Sanballat and Tobiah “that a man had come to seek טוֹבָה for the sons of Israel”.
“In the day of טוֹבָה be in good, and in the day of רָעָה consider: God has made the one as well as the other.”
“When goods (הַטּוֹבָה) increase, those who eat them increase.”
“To see the טוֹבָה of your chosen.”
“You crown the year of your טוֹבָה”: the harvest.
“You are my Lord; my טוֹבָה is not apart from you.”

senses.definition: To someone’s good, with a good purpose or outcome: God’s eye on a people “for good”, a plan turned “to good”, Nehemiah’s prayer to be remembered “for good”.

evidence.note: Joseph: “You meant evil against me; God meant it לְטֹבָה, to keep many people alive.”
Of the exiles: “I will set my eyes on them לְטוֹבָה and bring them back to this land.” Also Jer 24:5.
“I have set my face against this city לְרָעָה and not לְטוֹבָה.” Also Jer 39:16; 44:27; Amo 9:4.
“Remember me, my God, לְטוֹבָה.” Also Neh 5:19.
“The hand of our God is on all who seek him לְטוֹבָה.”

senses.gloss: the good (God) has promised or done
senses.definition: The good Yahweh has spoken concerning someone and brings about: his promise and its fulfilment.

evidence.note: David: “Your words are truth, and you have spoken this הַטּוֹבָה to your servant”: the promise of a house and a throne established forever.
“When Yahweh has done for my lord according to all הַטּוֹבָה he has spoken concerning you, and appointed you ruler over Israel.”
“As I brought all this great evil on this people, so I will bring on them all הַטּוֹבָה that I am speaking concerning them.”
The nations “will hear of all הַטּוֹבָה that I do for them”.
The people went home glad “for all הַטּוֹבָה Yahweh had done for David his servant and for Israel his people”.
“Every good word (הַדָּבָר הַטּוֹב) has come upon you”: here the adjective with דָּבָר; also Jos 21:45; Jer 29:10; 33:14.

evidence.locator: Neh.13.31, טוֹבָה → ἀγαθωσύνην; Jdg.9.16, 2Ch.24.16, Ecc.5.10 the same; ἀγαθωσύνη renders טוֹבָה ×10

evidence.note: Among the fruit of the spirit, ἀγαθωσύνη; the Peshitta has ܛܒܘܬܐ, this root.
“The fruit of the light is in all ἀγαθωσύνῃ and righteousness and truth.”

evidence.locator: Gen.50.20, לְטֹבָה → εἰς ἀγαθά; Neh.2.10, טוֹבָה → ἀγαθόν; ἀγαθός renders טוֹבָה ×42

evidence.note: “All things work together εἰς ἀγαθόν for those who love God”: the לְטוֹבָה of Gen 50:20.

words.gloss: be good, pleasing; be well (with); be glad; (hiphil) do good, do well
words.summary: The verb of the root in its own spelling: in the qal, to be good or pleasing, for it to be well with someone, and of the heart to be merry; in the hiphil, a few forms spelled without the י of יָטַב, to do good or do well. Most of the qal’s forms are spelled as the adjective, and the database counts them together.

stems.gloss: be good, pleasing; be well with; be glad

senses.definition: Be good or lovely to see; please someone, be good in his eyes.

evidence.note: Balaam: “מַה־טֹּבוּ your tents, Jacob, your dwellings, Israel!”
“How beautiful (יָּפוּ) is your love … how much טֹּבוּ your love than wine.”
“All the people noticed, and it was good in their eyes, as everything the king did טוֹב in the eyes of all the people.”
“Let him do to me as טוֹב in his eyes.”

senses.definition: Impersonally, “it is good to/for” someone: he fares well, it is to his good.

evidence.note: “You wept, saying, ‘Who will feed us flesh? For טוֹב לָנוּ in Egypt.’”
A servant who will not go free, “because he loves you and your house, because טוֹב לוֹ with you”.
David’s playing on the lyre: “and טוֹב לָךְ”, you will be well.
Put away innocent blood from Israel, “and it will be well with you”.
“טוֹב לִי that I was afflicted, that I might learn your statutes.”

senses.definition: With לֵב, to be glad or merry, usually with feasting and wine.

evidence.note: “Nabal’s heart was טוֹב within him, and he was very drunk.”
“When Amnon’s heart is טוֹב with wine.”
“When the heart of the king was טוֹב with wine.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, to do good to his people.

evidence.note: “You are good, וּמֵטִיב, and do good.”
“הֵיטִיבָה, Yahweh, to the good.”
“Do good to Zion in your favour; build the walls of Jerusalem.”
“I will rejoice over them לְהֵטִיב them, and plant them in this land in truth.”
“I will do better (וְהֵטִבֹתִי) than at your beginnings.”

senses.definition: To act rightly or skilfully.

evidence.note: Yahweh to David: “Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, הֱטִיבֹתָ, you did well, that it was in your heart.” Also 2Ch 6:8.
To Jehu: “Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes.”
“Like a love song, beautiful of voice and וּמֵטִב at playing.”

words.gloss: good things, goods, the best; goodness (of Yahweh); gladness
words.summary: An abstract noun: the good things of a land or house, its best; Yahweh’s goodness, shown in his bounty and declared with his name; and “goodness of heart”, gladness.

senses.gloss: good things, goods; the best (of a land)
senses.definition: The good things one has or eats: goods to take or give, the best of a land, its produce; and prosperity.

evidence.note: Pharaoh: “I will give you טוּב the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.”
“טוּב all the land of Egypt is yours.”
The servant took “all טוּב of his master” in his hand.
“Houses full of all טוּב which you did not fill.”
“If you are willing and obey, you shall eat טוּב the land.”
“I brought you into a land of plenty, to eat its fruit and its טוּב.”
“That you may eat טוּב the land and leave it to your sons forever.”
“Their prosperity (טוּבָם) is not in their hand.”
“When it goes well with the righteous (בְּטוּב צַדִּיקִים), the city rejoices.”
“I passed over טוּב her neck”: Ephraim’s fair neck, as a heifer’s.

senses.definition: Yahweh’s goodness: what he is and what he gives, his bounty to his people in the land and the good stored up for those who fear him.

evidence.note: To Moses, who asked to see his glory: “I will make all my טוּב pass before you, and proclaim the name Yahweh before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious.” The name proclaimed follows in Exo 34:6–7.
“How great is your טוּב, which you have stored up for those who fear you.”
“Unless I had believed to see טוּב Yahweh in the land of the living.”
“They shall pour forth the memory of your great טוּב.”
“I will recount the חֲסָדִים of Yahweh … and the great טוּב to the house of Israel, which he has given them according to his compassion.”
The returned “shall flow to טוּב Yahweh, to grain and new wine and oil, and to the young of flock and herd”.
“My people shall be satisfied with my טוּב.”
“Afterward the sons of Israel will return and seek Yahweh their God and David their king, and come in fear to Yahweh and to his טוּב in the latter days.”
“They delighted themselves in your great טוּב.” Also Neh 9:35.
“Remember me according to your חֶסֶד, for your טוּב’s sake, Yahweh.”
“We shall be satisfied with the טוּב of your house.”
“May you see the טוּב of Jerusalem all the days of your life.”
“How great is his טוּב, and how great his beauty!”

senses.definition: טוּב לֵב, goodness of heart: gladness.

evidence.note: “Because you did not serve Yahweh your God with joy and with טוּב לֵבָב for the abundance of all things.”
“My servants shall sing for טוּב לֵב, but you shall cry for pain of heart.”

senses.definition: In טוּב טַעַם, good discernment.

evidence.note: “Teach me טוּב טַעַם and knowledge, for I have believed your commandments.”

evidence.locator: Gen.45.18, טוּב → ἀγαθῶν; Psa.27.13, טוּב → ἀγαθά; Hos.3.5, טוּבוֹ → ἀγαθοῖς

evidence.note: “You received your τὰ ἀγαθά in your lifetime.”

words.gloss: be good, go well, please; (hiphil) do good, do right, do well, make good
words.summary: The verb of the root as spelled with initial י, which supplies its imperfect and hiphil (יִיטַב, הֵיטִיב). The qal is to be good or go well, and to please; the hiphil to do good to someone, to do right, to do a thing well or thoroughly (its infinitive הֵיטֵב is used as “well, thoroughly”), and to set a thing in order. Moses’ promise to Hobab uses it twice (Num 10:29, 32).

stems.gloss: be good, go well; be pleasing; (of the heart) be merry

senses.definition: Impersonally, for it to be well with someone: in Deuteronomy the promise attached to keeping Yahweh’s commandments.

evidence.note: “Honour your father and your mother … that your days may be long and that it may go well (יִיטַב) with you on the land Yahweh your God gives you.” Quoted Eph 6:2–3.
“Keep his statutes … that it may go well with you and your sons after you, and that you may prolong your days on the land.”
“Oh that they had such a heart … that it might go well with them and their sons forever.”
“Do the right and good in the eyes of Yahweh, that it may go well with you, and you may go in and possess the good land.”
“Obey my voice, and I will be your God … walk in all the way I command you, that it may go well with you.”
“Whether good or evil, we will obey the voice of Yahweh our God … that it may go well with us.”
Abram: “Say you are my sister, that it may go well with me because of you.”
Naomi: “Shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?”

senses.gloss: be good in the eyes of, please
senses.definition: Of a word, plan or person, to be good in someone’s eyes: to please him and win his approval.

evidence.note: “The word was good (וַיִּיטַב) in the eyes of Pharaoh and of all his servants.”
“The word was good in the eyes of the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.”
Aaron, after his sons’ death: “If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of Yahweh?”
“Moses heard, and it was good in his eyes.”
David “was good in the eyes of all the people”.
“The young woman was good in his eyes, and she won his favour.”
Praise “will please Yahweh more than an ox, a bull with horns and hoofs”.

senses.definition: With לֵב, to be glad, usually with food and drink.

evidence.note: “Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was merry (וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ).”
“Stay the night, and let your heart be merry.”
“The priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod.”
Jezebel to Ahab: “Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be merry.”
“By sadness of face the heart is made good.”

stems.gloss: do good (to); do right; do well, thoroughly; make good, set in order

senses.definition: To do good to someone, benefit him; often of Yahweh to his people, and of men repaying good.

evidence.note: Moses to Hobab: “Come with us, and we will do you good (וְהֵטַבְנוּ לָךְ), for Yahweh has spoken good concerning Israel.”
“That good which Yahweh will do (יֵיטִיב) with us, the same we will do (וְהֵטַבְנוּ) to you.”
Jacob: “You said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your seed as the sand of the sea.’” Also Gen 32:10.
Pharaoh “dealt well with Abram for her sake”.
“God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied.”
The manna, “to humble you and to test you, to do you good in your latter end”.
“As Yahweh rejoiced over you to do you good and multiply you, so he will rejoice over you to destroy you.”
“He will turn and do you evil and consume you, after he has done you good.”
Micah: “Now I know that Yahweh will do me good, since I have a Levite as priest.”
“An everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good.”
“So again I have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem.”
“Do not my words do good to him who walks uprightly?”
He “does no good to the widow”.
“I will relent of the good with which I said I would benefit (לְהֵיטִיב) it.”

senses.gloss: do right, do good; amend (one’s ways)
senses.definition: To do what is good and right, the opposite of doing evil; with “your ways”, to make them good, amend them.

evidence.note: To Cain: “If you do well (תֵּיטִיב), is there not a lifting up? And if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door.”
“Learn to do good (הֵיטֵב); seek justice, set right the oppressor, judge the orphan, plead for the widow.”
“Can the Cushite change his skin or the leopard his spots? Then you also can do good who are taught to do evil.”
“They are wise to do evil, but to do good they do not know.”
“Make good (הֵיטִיבוּ) your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.” Also Jer 7:5; 18:11; 26:13; 35:15.
The wicked “has ceased to be wise and to do good”.
Of idols: “they cannot do evil, and doing good is not in them either”.
“Do good or do evil, that we may be dismayed.”
Those who say in their heart, “Yahweh will not do good, nor will he do evil.”
Swearing rashly “to do evil or to do good”.

senses.definition: To do a thing well or rightly, or to say well; the infinitive הֵיטֵב after another verb means “well, thoroughly, diligently”.

evidence.note: When the people asked not to hear Yahweh’s voice again: “They have done well (הֵיטִיבוּ) in what they have spoken”, and he promises a prophet like Moses.
“You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to do it.”
“Do you do well (הַהֵיטֵב) to be angry?” Also Jon 4:9.
The calf: “I ground it, grinding thoroughly (הֵיטֵב), until it was fine as dust.”
“Write on the stones all the words of this law, very plainly (בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב).”
“Inquire and search and ask diligently.” Also Deu 17:4; 19:18.
Baal’s altars and images “they broke in pieces thoroughly”.
“Sing to him a new song; play skilfully (הֵיטִיבוּ נַגֵּן) with a shout.”
“A man who plays well.”
“Three things are stately in their step (מֵיטִיבֵי צָעַד).”
“The tongue of the wise uses knowledge well.”
“Their hands are on evil, to do it well.”
“How well you make your way to seek love.”
“Are you better than No-amon?”

senses.gloss: make good, make better; set in order, adorn; make glad
senses.definition: To make a thing good or better: to dress the lamps, adorn the head, make pillars goodly, make one’s name or kindness better; and of the heart, to make it glad.

evidence.note: Aaron burns incense morning by morning “when he dresses (בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ) the lamps”: makes them ready.
Jezebel “painted her eyes and adorned (וַתֵּיטֶב) her head”.
“According to the goodness of his land they made goodly (הֵיטִיבוּ) pillars.”
“May God make the name of Solomon better than your name.”
“You have made your last חֶסֶד better than the first.”
“A joyful heart makes healing good, but a broken spirit dries the bones.”
“A glad heart makes a cheerful face.”
“Let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth.”
“As they were making their hearts merry.”

opposites.note: Hiphil of רעע, “do evil”, set against הֵיטִיב: “do good or do evil”.

phrases.gloss: that it may go well with you
and it was good in the eyes of: it pleased

evidence.locator: Deu.4.40, יִיטַב → εὖ; Deu.6.18 the same; Num.10.29 and Num.10.32, הֵטַבְנוּ → εὖ; εὖ renders יָטַב ×21

evidence.note: Quoting the fifth commandment (Deu 5:16): “that it may be εὖ with you and you may live long on the earth”.

evidence.locator: Num.10.32, יֵיטִיב → ἀγαθοποιήσῃ; Zep.1.12, יֵיטִיב → ἀγαθοποιήσῃ

evidence.note: “Love your enemies and do good (ἀγαθοποιεῖτε)”; the Peshitta has the aphel of ܛܐܒ, this root.
God “did not leave himself without witness, doing good (ἀγαθοποιῶν), giving rains and fruitful seasons”.

words.summary: A noun from יָטַב, always in the construct: the best part of a land, field or flock. Six uses.

senses.gloss: the best (of a land, field, flock)
senses.definition: The best part of something, what is chosen out of it as finest.

evidence.note: Pharaoh: “Settle your father and your brothers in מֵיטַב the land; let them live in Goshen.” Also Gen 47:11.
He whose beast grazes another’s field “shall repay from מֵיטַב his field and מֵיטַב his vineyard”.
Saul and the people spared Agag “and מֵיטַב the sheep and the oxen … and all that was טוֹב”, destroying only what was despised.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once: the king’s gladness at Daniel’s deliverance.

senses.definition: Of the heart, to be glad, as Hebrew טוֹב לֵב.

evidence.note: “Then the king was very glad (שַׂגִּיא טְאֵב עֲלוֹהִי) and commanded that Daniel be taken up out of the den.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic’s adjective, twice: fine gold, and the courtier’s “if it is good to the king”, as in Hebrew.

senses.definition: Of fine quality.

evidence.note: “The head of that image was of דְהַב טָב, fine gold.”

senses.definition: In the formula of a request to a king, “if it is good to the king”.

evidence.note: “If it is טָב to the king, let search be made in the king’s treasure house.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once, in Artaxerxes’ letter to Ezra.

senses.definition: To please, to be thought best by someone.

evidence.note: “Whatever seems good (יֵיטַב) to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do according to the will of your God.”

words.gloss: good; (feminine as noun) good, a good thing; (adverb) very
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܒܐ (ṭābā), for ἀγαθός, καλός and χρηστός; its feminine ܛܒܬܐ is “good, a good thing”. Used as an adverb, ܛܒ is “very, greatly” (Mat 2:10), a use the Hebrew does not have.

senses.definition: Good in the full sense, which Jesus says belongs to God alone; and the Lord tasted as good.

evidence.note: “Why do you call me ܛܒܐ? There is none ܛܒܐ but one, God.” Also Mrk 10:18.
“If you have tasted and seen that the Lord is ܛܒ”: the Peshitta keeps Psa 34:9’s “taste and see”.

senses.gloss: good (as done, as announced); good and evil
senses.definition: The good done or brought, set against evil.

evidence.note: “Let him turn from evil and do ܛܒܬܐ”: Psa 34:15.
“There is none who does ܛܒܬܐ”: Psa 14:3.
“Those who bring good news of ܛܒܬܐ”: Isa 52:7.
“To discern ܛܒܬܐ and ܒܝܫܬܐ”, good and evil.
God “doing ܛܒܬܐ to them from heaven, sending rain”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܝܒܘܬܐ (ṭaybūtā), its word for χάρις, “grace”: a noun of this root, goodness shown to someone. SEDRA glosses it “grace; goodness; favour; kindness”.

senses.definition: God’s goodness and kindness shown freely to those who have not earned it, by which they are justified and saved.

evidence.note: “The law was given by the hand of Moses, but truth and ܛܝܒܘܬܐ came by Jesus the Messiah.”
“Full of ܛܝܒܘܬܐ and truth.”
“Justified freely (ܡܓܢ) by ܛܝܒܘܬܐ, through the redemption that is in Jesus the Messiah.”
“By his ܛܝܒܘܬܐ we are saved, through faith, and this is not of yourselves; it is the gift of God.”
“You have found ܛܝܒܘܬܐ with God.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܘܒܐ (ṭūbā), “blessedness”, used with a pronoun suffix for the Greek μακάριος: ܛܘܒܝܗܘܢ, “blessed are they”. Hebrew says this with אַשְׁרֵי, another root; the Peshitta’s idiom, like the Targums’ טוּבֵי, uses this one.

senses.definition: An exclamation of someone’s good estate, “O the blessedness of…!”

evidence.note: “ܛܘܒܝܗܘܢ to the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven”; so through Mat 5:11.
Quoting Psa 32:1, where the Hebrew is אַשְׁרֵי: “ܛܘܒܝܗܘܢ whose iniquities are forgiven.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܒܘܬܐ (ṭābūtā), for ἀγαθωσύνη, twice.

senses.definition: Goodness as a quality of life, fruit of the spirit and of the light.

evidence.note: Among the fruit of the spirit: love, joy, peace … ܛܒܘܬܐ, faith.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܝܒ (ṭayyeb), for ἑτοιμάζω: to make a thing ready. How “make ready” comes from “good” is shown by the Hebrew hiphil of יָטַב, which dresses lamps and adorns a head (Exo 30:7; 2Ki 9:30), and by Akkadian ṭiābu, “make good, make suitable, repair”: to make good is to put in order.

senses.definition: To get a way, a place or a meal ready.

evidence.note: “Prepare (ܛܝܒܘ) the way of the Lord”: Isa 40:3, where the Hebrew has פַּנּוּ, another root.
“I go to prepare a place for you.” Also Jhn 14:3.
“Where do you want us to prepare the Passover for you?”
“The disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and prepared the Passover.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܛܐܒ in the aphel, “do good”, for ἀγαθοποιέω, twice in Luke 6.

senses.definition: To do good to others, enemies included.

evidence.note: “Love your enemies, and do good (ܘܐܛܐܒܘ) to them, and lend.”

cognates.gloss: be good, pleasant, sweet, fragrant; be pure; (of the soul) be glad, willing; good, pleasant, wholesome, pure
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give the verb as “the contr. of خَبِيث” (bad, foul): “good, pleasant, delightful, delicious, sweet, or savoury … in taste, and in odour”, and “pure, or clean”; طَابَتْ نَفْسُهُ “his mind was cheerful, happy, pleased”; the adjective of food, sweet water, a fertile land, a good house, and pleasant dispositions. This answers to טוֹב of food, land and fruit set against רַע, to the glad heart (טוֹב לֵב), and to what pleases. Lane files the root with medial y; Hebrew and Aramaic have medial w (טוב) beside initial y (יטב), and Lane also records a dialect form أَيْطَبُ for أَطْيَبُ.

evidence.locator: p. 1900, root طيب, طَابَ (n27402)
SEM000502 ṭwb [good], ARB019803 TaAba [good], HEB002677 ṭowb [good]

cognates.gloss: better, best; (plural) the best parts of a thing
cognates.note: The elative of ṭayyib, “better, and best”; its plural أَطَايِبُ (and مَطَايِبُ) “the best, or best parts, of a thing, as of flesh-meat”, “the best of fresh ripe dates”, “the best portions of the herbage”. This answers to מֵיטָב, “the best of” a land or flock, and to טוֹב מִן, “better than”.

cognates.gloss: good fortune, a good final state; blessedness
cognates.note: Lane: an infinitive noun of ṭāba, “a good final, or ultimate, state or condition”, “good, good fortune”, “God’s blessing or favour”, “a pleasant life”. The same form and use as the Syriac ܛܘܒܐ, “blessedness”, of the Beatitudes.

cognates.gloss: good, pleasant, sweet, aromatic, favourable, friendly; be(come) good, be pleasing, do well, improve, make good
cognates.note: The adjective is among the commonest Akkadian words (Oracc counts 5769 instances). The verb ṭiābu covers “be pleasing”, “do (something) well”, “make good, make suitable” and “improve”, the range of Hebrew יָטַב in qal and hiphil; with libbu, “heart”, libba ṭiābu is “be(come) satisfied”, as Hebrew’s heart that is טוֹב.

evidence.locator: armep x000005880, ṭābu [good] AJ
armep x000020310, ṭiābu [be(come) good] V; armep x000154850, libba ṭiābu [be(come) satisfied] V

cognates.gloss: goodness, favour, good deed(s), good relations, friendship
cognates.note: The feminine noun, as Hebrew טוֹבָה: good done to someone, a favour, and good relations between parties. Hebrew sets “their peace and their טוֹבָה” together (Deu 23:7), and Oracc’s glosses for ṭābtu include “peace”. Not ṭabtu “salt”, a different word.

evidence.locator: tsae x000004140, ṭābtu [goodness] N

cognates.note: The same pattern as Hebrew טוּב, with the same senses of goodness and well-being; ṭūb libbi, “goodness of heart”, contentment, is Hebrew’s טוּב לֵב (Deu 28:47; Isa 65:14).

evidence.locator: armep x000036240, ṭūbu [goodness] N
armep x000150060, ṭūb libbi [mental well-being] N

cognates.note: Segert’s glossary gives ṭb /ṭāb-/ “good”, comparing Aramaic ṭab, Akkadian ṭābu and Hebrew ṭôb, and in the wine list KTU 4.213:2 “spiced (wine)”, comparing Song of Songs 7:10, “like the טוֹב wine”. The grammar’s §65 cites “yn d l ṭb”, “wine which is not good”, from the same text.

Old South Arabian (Sabaic): the noun ṭyb names a kind of “sweet” incense, written on incense burners beside nard, and the adjective ṭybm is “sweet-smelling”. Biella compares Arabic ṭayyib “sweet-scented” and ṭīb “perfume”. It shows the root’s sense of what is pleasant to the senses, as in Hebrew טוֹב of wine and ointment (Sng 1:3; 7:10; Ecc 7:1). OCR text read; page image not checked.

cognates.gloss: be good, be well, fare well; (aphel) do good; good, precious
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums: the verb טַב (contracted from טאב) “to be good, well”, טב ל־ “to feel well, be satisfied, fare well” (Targ. Deu 15:16, for Hebrew טוֹב לוֹ), aphel “to do good”; and the adjective טַב, טָבָא “good, precious” (Targ. Gen 2:9). Jastrow also gives pael טַיֵּיב and aphel אָטֵיב “to do good, to favour”. Aramaic has both the טאב/טוב form and יְטַב, as Biblical Aramaic does (Dan 6:24; Ezr 7:18).

evidence.locator: s.v. טַב I, טַב II
evidence.note: Targ. Deut. 15:16; Targ. Zech. 12:4; Targ. Gen. 2:9.

evidence.locator: s.v. טוֹב (Pa. טַיֵּיב, Af. אָטֵיב)
evidence.note: Targ. Y. I Ex. 23:2.

cognates.gloss: good, goodness, mercy; (plural construct) happy!, blessed! (for Hebrew אַשְׁרֵי)
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: “good, goodness, mercy” (Targ. Isa 1:19, for טוּב הָאָרֶץ), and in the plural construct “happiness, used like אַשְׁרֵי, happy!, blessed!” (Targ. Ps 1:1; Targ. 1Ki 10:8). The same idiom as the Peshitta’s ܛܘܒܝܗܘܢ, “blessed are they”.

evidence.locator: s.v. טוּבָא
evidence.note: Targ. Is. 1:19; Targ. Ps. 33:22; Targ. I Kings 10:8; Targ. Ps. 1:1.

doctrine.statement: On each day of creation God sees what he has made “that it was טוֹב”, and on the sixth day he sees everything he has made, “and behold, טוֹב מְאֹד” (Gen 1:4–31). The one thing called “not good” is the man alone, and God at once makes the woman (Gen 2:18–22). Death comes into the account only as the sentence on disobedience: “in the day you eat of it you shall surely die”, “dust you are, and to dust you shall return” (Gen 2:17; 3:19). Paul says that “by one man sin entered the world, and death by sin” (Rom 5:12), and that “by man came death” (1Co 15:21); and he still calls “every creature of God καλόν”, the Greek of Gen 1’s טוֹב (1Ti 4:4). From the verses: the world God finished in the six days was very good, with no death in it; death came afterward, by man’s sin, and not as part of the making.

The tree of “the knowledge of טוֹב וָרָע” was forbidden on pain of death (Gen 2:9, 17); the serpent promised that eating it would make them “like God, knowing טוֹב וָרָע” (Gen 3:5), and afterward Yahweh says “the man has become like one of us, to know טוֹב וָרָע” (Gen 3:22). Elsewhere, knowing good and evil is what little children do not yet do (Deu 1:39; Isa 7:15–16) and what a king must do to judge, “like the angel of God” (2Sa 14:17); Solomon asks it of God as “a hearing heart … to discern between טוֹב and רָע” (1Ki 3:9). Hebrews makes it the mark of maturity, “senses trained to discern good and evil” (Heb 5:14), and the psalmist asks God to teach him good discernment (Psa 119:66, 68). From the verses: to know good and evil is to judge for oneself what is good and what is bad. Rightly it is asked of God and learned from his word; in Eden man took it for himself against his word.

The temple’s refrain is “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is טוֹב, for his חֶסֶד is forever” (Psa 136:1; 1Ch 16:34; Ezr 3:11). His goodness is seen in what he does: “You are טוֹב and do good” (Psa 119:68); “Yahweh is טוֹב to all, and his compassion is over all his works” (Psa 145:9). When Moses asked to see his glory, Yahweh said “I will make all my טוּב pass before you, and proclaim the name Yahweh before you” (Exo 33:19), and the name proclaimed is “Yahweh, Yahweh, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in חֶסֶד and truth, … who will by no means clear the guilty” (Exo 34:6–7). Jesus says, “No one is good but one, God” (Mat 19:17; Mrk 10:18). From the verses: goodness in its full sense is God’s own character, declared in his name and shown in his deeds; men are good as they do what he shows them is good (Mic 6:8).

The Peshitta’s word for χάρις, grace, is ܛܝܒܘܬܐ (ṭaybūtā), a noun of this root: “the law was given by the hand of Moses, but truth and ṭaybūtā came by Jesus the Messiah” (Jhn 1:17); “justified freely by his ṭaybūtā” (Rom 3:24); “by his ṭaybūtā you are saved, through faith … it is the gift of God” (Eph 2:8). In the Hebrew, Yahweh’s טוּב passing before Moses comes with “I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious” and the name “merciful and gracious … abundant in חֶסֶד and truth” (Exo 33:19; 34:6), which John’s “grace and truth” answers (Jhn 1:14, 17). From the verses: in the apostles’ own language grace is God’s goodness, the good he does to those who have not earned it.

Moses urges Hobab to come with Israel “to the place of which Yahweh said, I will give it to you … for Yahweh has spoken טוֹב concerning Israel” (Num 10:29); the good Yahweh has spoken is his promise of the land. Joshua says “not one word failed of all the good word (הַדָּבָר הַטּוֹב) Yahweh spoke to the house of Israel” (Jos 21:45; 23:14–15). David calls the promise of a house and a kingdom established forever “this הַטּוֹבָה” (2Sa 7:16, 28). Through Jeremiah Yahweh says “I will perform the good word (הַדָּבָר הַטּוֹב) that I have spoken to the house of Israel and the house of Judah: in those days … I will cause a Branch of righteousness to grow up to David” (Jer 33:14–15), and the one who “brings good news of טוֹב” says to Zion “your God reigns” (Isa 52:7), words Paul applies to the preaching of the gospel (Rom 10:15). From the verses: “the good” God speaks is his promise, of the land, of David’s house and kingdom, and of the righteous Branch from David; the good news is the announcement of that kingdom.

Moses calls Yahweh’s commandments given “לְטוֹב לָךְ, for your good” (Deu 10:13), and sets before Israel “life and טוֹב, death and רָע” (Deu 30:15). The commands carry the promise “that it may go well (יִיטַב) with you, and that you may prolong your days on the land” (Deu 4:40; 5:16), and Paul repeats the fifth commandment with its promise to children in the ecclesia: “that it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth” (Eph 6:2–3). Jeremiah: “Obey my voice … that it may go well with you” (Jer 7:23). Joseph says of what his brothers did, “you meant evil against me; God meant it לְטֹבָה” (Gen 50:20), and Paul: “all things work together for good to those who love God” (Rom 8:28). From the verses: God’s law is given for the good of those who keep it, and what he purposes for those who love him is their good.
